memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When you reached this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to fight against us, but we defeated them. We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh." — Deut 29:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses continues the roll call of remembrance, now recalling recent victories — the defeats of Sihon and Og, two powerful kings who came out to fight and were overthrown. Their lands became an inheritance for the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh. These were fresh, tangible proofs that God gives His people victory and keeps His promises.

Notice the pattern in Moses' preaching. He does not only point to the distant past of Egypt; he points to recent evidence too — battles won just lately, promises freshly kept. God's faithfulness is not only ancient history; it is current reality.

This is a helpful practice for us. When we look back over our lives, we can trace both the long-ago mercies of our conversion and the recent, fresh victories God has given — the answered prayer last month, the strength He gave last week, the door He opened just yesterday. Both the distant and the recent testify to the same faithful God.

Every earthly victory God gave Israel pointed forward to the ultimate victory won in Christ. Through Him, God gives us the final triumph over sin and death, and an inheritance that can never perish (1 Pet 1:3-4). Sihon and Og fell; but the greater enemies — sin, death, and the grave — have fallen forever before our risen King. Remember the victories, both recent and eternal, and take heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can I recall both long-ago and recent evidences of God's faithfulness?
2. How does remembering God's victories build my confidence in Him?
3. What recent "victory" has God given me that I can thank Him for?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for the victories You have given, both long ago and only recently. Above all, thank You for the triumph over sin and death in Christ. Help me remember and take courage. Amen.
